title: James Gadson - Wikipedia
notes: James Edward Gadson, born 17 June 1939, Kansas City, Missouri; died 2 April 2026, aged 86 (Modern Drummer's obituary says 87). 'One of the most-recorded drummers in the history of R&B.' The first line-up of Charles Wright's Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band, three albums 1968-1970; Dyke & the Blazers; Bill Withers's Still Bill (1972); the Temptations' 1990 (1973); Freddie King, Martha Reeves, Randy Crawford, Quincy Jones, Herbie Hancock, B.B. King, Albert King, Rose Royce; Billy Griffin & the Miracles' City of Angels (1975); Marvin Gaye's I Want You, Diana Ross's Love Hangover and Thelma Houston's Don't Leave Me This Way (1976); Paul McCartney's Chaos and Creation in the Backyard (2005); Beck's Sea Change, The Information and Morning Phase; Jamie Lidell's Compass (2010); D'Angelo's Sugah Daddy (Black Messiah, 2014), drums and hambone. Also a singer and songwriter.

title: Still Bill - Wikipedia
notes: Bill Withers's second album, Sussex, 1 May 1972, recorded at the Record Plant, Los Angeles, 'with musicians from the Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band'; James Gadson drums and percussion, and co-producer. Lean on Me (number one, mid 1972) and Use Me (number two). Gold, 7 September 1972. Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums (2020), number 333.

title: Use Me (Bill Withers song) - Wikipedia
notes: On Still Bill (1972), single September 1972, number two on the Billboard Hot 100 and the soul chart. James Gadson, drums and percussion. An eight-minute live version opens Live at Carnegie Hall (1973).

title: Charles Wright & the Watts 103rd Street Rhythm Band - Wikipedia
notes: The band that settled by 1968 and played on every Watts 103rd album from then: drummer James Gadson, bassist Melvin Dunlap, trombonist and arranger Ray Jackson, guitarists Al McKay and Benorce Blackmon; several of them on Dyke and the Blazers' singles (1969). 'The middle ground between Otis Redding and James Brown' (Wright). Do Your Thing (1968), Express Yourself (Warner Bros., 1970). After You're So Beautiful (1971), Gadson, Dunlap, Jackson and Blackmon left to work with Bill Withers: Still Bill and Live at Carnegie Hall.

title: Shout It Out (Patrice Rushen album) - Wikipedia
notes: Patrice Rushen's third album and last for Prestige (1977): jazz, funk, fusion and R&B. James Gadson drums on tracks 1-7, 'right' drums on 8 (Graham Lear 'left').

title: Vulfpeck - Wikipedia
notes: Mr Finish Line (November 2017) 'featured veteran instrumentalists James Gadson, Bootsy Collins, Michael Bland, David T. Walker'. Vulfpeck modelled on the session players of the 1960s: recorded live, seldom cut together.

title: All the grooves from Still Bill (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 18 December 2011)
notes: Two engraved pages, a groove for each track: Lonely Town, Lonely Street (82, 'swing the 16th notes'), Who Is He (96), Use Me (73, the snare as a cross-stick), Lean on Me (68, verse and chorus), Kissing My Love (90, 'half-swing 16ths'), I Don't Know (92, floor tom with a mallet, brushes overdubbed), Another Day to Run (112), I Don't Want You on My Mind (12/8, 77), Take It All and Check It All Out (111). Notes in parentheses are ghosts or optional.

title: Transcription: James Gadson - Use Me (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 27 October 2011)
notes: The three drum breaks of Use Me, four bars each, marked 78. 'Not too strong on the accents'; 'Hi-hats half open where indicated'; 'the open hihat notes should just have a little sizzle to them.' The cross-stick and the kick in 16ths between the hats.

title: Transcription: James Gadson - Shout It Out (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 2018)
notes: 34 bars from 0:27, marked 78, up to where he moves to the ride. The PDF credits Ndugu Leon Chancler; the post corrects it to Gadson ('my CD says James Gadson'). 'A pretty classic 70s fusion/funk groove, with a displaced back beat and an open hihat on 4'; a five-piece kit with two added concert toms; fills 'about building the groove ... at an even volume and ... right on the 16th note pulse'.

title: James Gadson: soul master (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 4 February 2011)
notes: Clips: Bill Withers, Dyke & the Blazers, a Ramsey Lewis session, the documentary Keep in Time 'also featuring Earl Palmer and Paul Humphrey'. A commenter: 'a clinic on use of the kick, hats and snare'; another on his instructional video, made in Japan.

title: Legendäre Drummer & Grooves #6: James Gadson (Bonedo, 2018; transcription by Harry Bum Tschak)
notes: Vulfpeck's Running Away (Mr Finish Line, 2017), marked 81: the intro and verse on kick and rim click with an accent on the rack tom, no hat; the bridge on the snare with eighths on the hat; the second chorus in 16ths on the hat, accented on '4+' and sometimes '2+'. 'The kick plays a Motown pattern'; snare and tom muffled with towels; soft, dry and warm. Recommended listening from Express Yourself (1967-1970) to D'Angelo's Black Messiah (2014).

title: Bill Withers: 'Use Me' - James Gadson Drum Groove (Bart Elliott, Drummer Cafe, 15 December 2010)
notes: 'Originally played at 77-78 bpm, with straight sixteenth-notes on the HiHat and linear, quasi-paradiddle figures between the Snare (cross-stick) and Kick drum.' 'Playing in the cracks ... between a straight and swung feel'; 'Gadson's feel is actually very close to a straight sixteenth, more so than actually swung.'

title: Behind The Beat: The Drumming Style Of James Gadson (Melodics)
notes: Read only through a search engine's excerpt (the page body did not load): 'Gadson's kick drum is unwavering while his hi-hats and rimclicks are often fractionally behind or ahead of the beat.' A Melodics lesson author who turned his loops to MIDI found his hi-hat swing consistent and the kick 'solid and on beat'.
